column1: # r-zig stress suite: one row per target, run in file order (cheap groups first).
# stress.R reads this file; stress/README.md explains the suite.
#   package     CRAN/Bioconductor name, or name:variant (a second install of the
#               same package with other env vars, into a library of its own)
#   group       g3 C libraries from the env, g4 own build systems / bundled code,
#               g2 C++ across a library boundary, g1 heavy C++ (the brief's 1-4)
#   tags        extra labels a target or --skip can name: heavy (long builds,
#               e.g. `--skip=heavy` on small CI runners); name@os limits one
#   oses        all, or a comma list of linux, macos, windows
#   sysdeps     conda-forge names the row needs in the libraries env;
#               name@os limits one to an OS. For documentation, the drift
#               check against the env's conda-meta, and the --conda env.
#   env         NAME=VALUE;NAME=VALUE set for this row only; {env} is the
#               libraries env dir (its Library on Windows)
#   expect      one value, or os=value pairs: ok, fail-abi, fail-sysdep,
#               dependency failed), ? (no guess). A guess until a run
#   smoke       one R expression run after library(); FALSE or an error fails
#               it; must not need the network. The runner then unloads the
#               namespace and checks R's exit. The file stays ASCII: write
#   note        why the row is here, what it exercises
